chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: The stage director says darkies and Mae West demands an apology
summary: In Atlantic City the white stage manager said get the darkies together, so Olive Burgorne got Mae West to make him apologize.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So what happened with that? So you got in this show What was the name of that show?

The Constant Sinner. So we had a rehearsal in the day, and after the first week we go to the Brighton Theatre in Brighton Beach -- that's near Coney Island. That's where the show opened for the tryout, and then we go to Atlantic City for a week.
And at the rehearsal in...in the dress rehearsal in Atlantic City, we're all on the stage after the rehearsal, and the...
On stage after the rehearsal, and the stage manager did what?
He was an old Southerner, a middle-aged man -- to me he looked old. He had made a remark. He told somebody 'Get all the darkies together.'
Yeah. He was the stage manager. And Olive Burgorne(?) heard him. And she was a woman that, you know,

she don't go for nothin'. So she told Mae West, Olive said, "Well, I ain't gonna call 'em and I ain't gonna do nothin' until he apologizes." That's what she told Mae West. And Mae West came out of her dressing room and called him, and explained to him that his remarks about the Darkies... "There are no darkies here." Well, he laughed and he said, "Well, I didn't mean no harm." I thought it was a familiar thing that you say. Black people don't get angry about them kinds of things." She said, "Well, we do get angry up here, and don't use that remark no more." And she said, "You owe these people an apology." So he said, "I'll apologize. I'm very sorry." And he apologized.
